newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Yukong keeps reformer shut on low domestic demand.
newsitem.headline: Yukong keeps reformer shut on low domestic demand.

text.p: South Korean refiner Yukong Ltd has decided to keep its 8,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) reformer No.1 shut amid low domestic demand and weak petrochemical prices, an industry source said on Tuesday.
"We shut down No.1 until the end of March but if there's no improvement, we will extend it," the source said.
The secondary refining unit which processes naphtha into reformate for either gasoline blending or further production into petrochemical BTX, was shut down January 24 due to poor margins.
"It does not make economics either for BTX production or as a gasoline blendstock," the source said.
"We have decided to sustain the shutdown....domestic gasoline demand is lower than expected this year, and the reformate price as compared to the naphtha is very weak," he said.
The source told Reuters domestic demand, currently 150,000-bpd, was 50,000-bpd lower than earlier projections.
"Usually we get some slight increase (in demand), but so far from January to end-February, it has decreased," he said. "Most Korean refiners tried to export in February."
Yukong, for the first time, sold a 250,000-barrel cargo of 95-octane unleaded reformate into Taiwan's import tender for second-half March delivery.
